clue.text: Hope it didn't break when Tony Benn dropped it

definitions.meaning: a piece of fine English pottery is something you hope does not break
the politician was born Anthony ... Benn and dropped the middle name to become plain Tony Benn

explanation.surface: Someone fears a breakage at the moment a famous politician let something fall.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Benn, a British Labour politician, shed his double-barrelled style; the same name belongs to the famous Staffordshire pottery firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a renowned brand of English china and the middle name the politician abandoned.

clue.text: Confuse whelk with music accompanying farewell to setter

indicators.note: to confuse things is to mix them up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone muddles a shellfish with a tune while saying goodbye to the compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confuse' jumbles WHELK and MUSIC together; 'with' and 'accompanying' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking for good fortune is a parting phrase the setter would hear as a send-off.

clue.text: Explosive character subverts (bother!) one — lots — five hundred

indicators.note: subverts means overturns, so the whole string of pieces is read upside down in a down entry

parts.note: drat is a mild exclamation like bother
I is the Roman numeral for one
many means lots
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: An explosive figure overturns one item after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subverts' turns the whole run DRATIMANYD backwards; the bracket and dashes just separate the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamitard is someone who uses dynamite, a bomber, so an explosive person.

clue.text: Cautious about model being flawed

indicators.note: about places the word for cautious around the model

parts.note: wary means cautious
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so T can stand for model

explanation.surface: A careful person is concerned about a model being faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Warty means covered with warts, blemished, so flawed.

clue.text: Burns derived novel containing 11, they say

definitions.text: Burns derived novel containing 11, they say

parts.words: Burns derived novel containing 11, they say
parts.note: a Steinbeck novel takes its title from a line in Robert Burns's poem To a Mouse, and its middle sounds like the porcelain town Meissen

explanation.surface: A novel taken from a Scottish poet contains a famous china.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Burns was Scotland's national poet; 11 is Dresden china, also called Meissen, which the title's middle words resemble when spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Steinbeck named the novel after the Burns line about schemes of mice and men going awry.

clue.text: Nasty party backing bills

indicators.note: backing means the word for party is turned round to run backwards

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
IOUs are written promises to pay, a kind of bill

explanation.surface: A political party gets support from unpleasant debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks political, but it is a do, a social party, and 'backing' turns it round to OD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odious is hateful and repugnant, a stronger synonym of nasty.

clue.text: Half 11 right away with island girl who was stifled

indicators.note: away tells us the right letter is taken out

parts.note: half of the twelve letters of the answer to 11 down gives the first six
Mona is the old Latin name for Anglesey or the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Half of something goes with a girl from an island who was smothered.
explanation.walkthrough: Desdemona is the wife smothered by Othello in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello stifles his wife with a pillow, so the stifled girl is that heroine.

clue.text: Have covered lines with plenty of stitching

indicators.note: covered means the word for have wraps around the lines

parts.note: to own is to have
verse is lines of poetry

explanation.surface: A garment covered with lines has lots of needlework.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversewn means stitched over and over along an edge, so heavily stitched.

clue.text: Look round books and it reveals former email

indicators.note: round means the word for look goes about the other pieces

parts.note: to look a certain way is to seem
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: Searching through books turns up an old electronic message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look' is a verb of appearance, seem, not of seeing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sent item is a message already dispatched, so an email from the past.

clue.text: Erred (heard) going to capital with indications of problem

indicators.note: heard tells us that the word meaning erred is used only for how it is said

parts.note: to have erred is to have sinned
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Someone who went wrong heads off to a city with signs of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndrome is a set of symptoms, the signs that together point to a medical problem.

clue.text: Trailing flower's name

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A trailing plant has a name of its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailing' looks like a description of a creeping plant, but it means behind, as a boat's wake lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern means behind a ship, so something trailing behind is astern.

clue.text: Attractive figures of Judi dividing the odd sardine

indicators.note: dividing means the actress splits the other letters
odd signals that the letters of sardine are rearranged

parts.note: Judi Dench is the famous English actress

explanation.surface: An actress comes between people and an unusual fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges the fish to DRESINA; 'Judi' is the actress Dame Judi Dench, and 'Attractive figures' are pretty porcelain figurines, not a person's shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden china is decorative porcelain, famous for pretty figurines.

clue.text: Dam's dam, say, in pseudo horror film

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother, so dam's means mother's, which is mummy's
said aloud, dam is damn, and damn is a curse

explanation.surface: A mother animal's own mother appears in a mock horror movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The first dam is a mother, as in horse breeding; the second, with 'say', is heard as the oath damn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mummy's Curse is a classic title for the kind of schlock horror movie about an Egyptian mummy.

clue.text: Corrupter of insect (mature queen) at first

indicators.note: at first means the bracketed pieces are placed before the insect

parts.note: adult means grown up, mature
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Something that spoils an insect's mature queen first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' moves the bracketed mature queen to the front, though the insect is named first; ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulterant is a substance that contaminates or debases something, a corrupting agent.

clue.text: Ware of success for Queen's horse?

definitions.meaning: ware means pottery or china, here a fine porcelain
a royal horse winning the famous Epsom race would be a triumph for the monarchy

explanation.surface: Pottery commemorates a win by a royal racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is England's most famous flat horse race, run at Epsom; the crown stands for the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Crown Derby is a porcelain maker, and its name also reads as a monarch's Derby victory.

clue.text: Stop 19 rising

parts.note: the answer to 19 across is a verb meaning permit, which is let
rising means going up

explanation.surface: Halt the climb of clue 19.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-up is a pause or easing, a stop in something that was going on.

clue.text: Left book in case

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a folio is a large book

explanation.surface: A book left in a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a flat carrying case for papers or drawings.

clue.text: Truant sailor takes second turn right

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor

indicators.note: turn tells us the letters of second are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A runaway seaman takes a second right turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' looks like S, but it is the fodder itself: 'turn' rearranges SECOND to SCONDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An absconder runs away from where they should be, as a truant does from school.

clue.text: Vehicle for high pressure container

parts.note: a cart is a simple wheeled vehicle
in weather forecasts a ridge is an elongated area of high pressure

explanation.surface: Something to carry a container under heavy pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge is a small case holding ink, film or explosive, so a kind of container.

clue.text: Don't stop every cry of pain

parts.note: all is used here for every
ow is what you cry out when hurt

explanation.surface: Someone urges that every scream of pain should carry on.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow something is to permit it, not to stop it.

clue.text: Pain from stick?

parts.note: pain is the French word for bread, and a French stick is a long thin loaf

explanation.surface: Someone complains of the hurt a stick caused.
explanation.walkthrough: Pain is French for bread, not English hurt, and a stick here is a loaf, not a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A baguette, or French stick, is the loaf that French speakers call pain.

clue.text: First two to the dip?

parts.note: the first two letters of the alphabet are B and A
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people are first into the swim.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to swim or take a dip.

clue.text: See 8
See 7
Soprano Soprano Soprano

parts.note: one word for a boy's high singing voice also means three times over, as the clue's repetition shows

explanation.surface: Three high voices are listed one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy soprano is called a treble, and treble also means threefold, matching the triple repetition.

clue.text: Missile to expose to music

parts.note: to air something is to expose it to view or to fresh air
taken as written
an air is a tune, a piece of music

explanation.surface: A rocket is played to a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An air-to-air missile is one fired from one aircraft at another; the term names the weapon by its type.

clue.text: Pristine condition continuing like 1 across

parts.note: an item in mint condition is pristine, as if new
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: Something kept in perfect shape goes on like an earlier answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 across is a famous English pottery; this answer is another one, from Stoke-on-Trent.
explanation.definitionFit: Minton is another celebrated Staffordshire porcelain maker, so it is a ware of the same kind.

clue.text: Shelter in another play? How obvious can you get?

definitions.note: the question works as an exclamation meaning obviously, an adverb

indicators.note: in places the word for shelter within the rearranged letters
another version of the word play means its letters rearranged

parts.note: a tent is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: A tent features in a different play, and it could not be clearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' rearranges the letters of play to PALY; the question at the end is the setter's exclamation, standing for an adverb meaning obviously.
explanation.definitionFit: Patently means plainly or obviously, the sense the rhetorical question conveys.
